changelog: Weakened the automatic upward boost for cuts adjacent to numerals/ dates/ percentages/ names by adding an operational 'numeric-attachment' exception: when left_last contains a digit and right_first has tight numeric-unit surface shape (short lowercase alpha token, contains a digit, or contains %/currency characters), require higher lexical density on both sides to keep a high score; otherwise lower the bias. (Addresses measured over-trust on numeral+unit splits: en_us_66, en_us_278, en_us_203, en_us_140.)

Reduced the short-name/organization/place shortcut: short capitalized tokens at the cut (length ≤ 10) no longer automatically give a strong boost unless the left stretch contains ≥ 3 content tokens. This lowers upward bias on appositive short names that the critique flagged. (Addresses en_us_738, en_us_1000, en_us_276.)

Made comma-adjacent adjunct boosts more conservative by adding a continuity test: if a comma precedes the marker but the right_first looks like a participial continuation (surface ends with 'ing') and the right stretch is low in lexical content, reduce the upward bias. This treats many comma+participial continuations as less likely true adjunct boundaries unless lexical density supports them. (Addresses comma + 'ing' continuation errors noted in the summary.)

Operationalized 'lexical density' and 'content-token' checks as concrete surface heuristics (alphabetic tokens longer than 2 chars excluding a small stoplist). These counts are used in the three exceptions above so decisions remain surface-anchored and testable.

Rewrote the surface-form checklist to include the numeric-attachment and short-name exceptions and to make all heuristics explicitly testable with the immediately adjacent tokens and short counts of content tokens on each side.
